name: Mohamed Landolsi
positioning: I build outbound and research systems for B2B teams in n8n, Clay and custom APIs. Plain rules screen the data first, an LLM writes only from verified facts, and a person approves anything that leaves.
hero_headline_options: I build outbound systems that filter hard, write carefully and wait for a human.
Automation for go-to-market teams: the system does the screening, a person does the sending.
Most of a GTM workflow is saying no. I make the machine do that part.

about: I studied software engineering in Nabeul and spent my final six months at Wavess, a Berlin B2B SaaS startup, working on a platform that turns market signals into GTM actions for small B2B teams.

That internship taught me the part of GTM work nobody demos: most of the job is throwing away the wrong accounts, the wrong people and the wrong sentences before anything reaches a customer. Since then I have built two systems around that idea, both on free tiers, both running on my own data.
I write the decision down before I build the workflow. Every project here has its decision log, its telemetry and the bugs that changed it.

principles.title: Rules before models
principles.text: Plain rules screen every account before any model or paid call: domain, team size, industry, timezone, seen before. Spend stays predictable, and the model only sees what passed.

principles.title: Every provider has a fallback
principles.text: Each model call goes through a chain of providers set in config. A rate limit or an outage moves the call to the next model, and every failure is logged per provider.

principles.title: Telemetry before rewriting
principles.text: Every run writes its counters and error samples to an ops tab. Tuning is a config change with a revision number, one variable at a time, with the run that shows the effect.

principles.title: A person approves what leaves
principles.text: The system drafts messages but has no way to send them. I review each draft, edit or reject it, and send it myself.
